Meta has virtually all of its revenue from  advertising, coming from a variety of platforms, including Instagram. Meta invested heavily in AI infrastructure primarily to  develop the AI tools to improve customary engagement on these platforms and increase ad revenues.  Note, Meta owns proprietary data used to train the AI models and thus benefits from owning its'  own infrastructure - so Meta invested heavily in datacenters.  Based on the recent Meta earnings, this strategy worked well - the AI tools improved engagement and boosted ad revenues. I, personally, don't  like the AI-generated videos, but it looks like it works for other people.  However, now it appears that Meta overinvested in these datacenters - the compute capacity exceeds the demand for compute, as it relates to  Meta's ad business. Thus, Meta now needs to rent this excess compute capacity.
